Mira: Thinking about edgecases for a staged drain/soft-demote flow. If we keep residency for N seconds, what guarantees do we give for read-after-write during owner takeover?
Kai: Short answer: none by default unless we persist some drain marker visible to the new owner.
Noah: Persisting always is heavy. Could we instead snapshot the inflight refcount to the lease store only when inflight > threshold?
Mira: That hybrid makes sense: local-only for quick drains, durable marker for long drains or when refcount high.
Kai: Also consider a compact marker: epoch + inflight_estimate + expires_at. New owner can read estimate and delay final eviction if estimate>0.
Noah: How do writers behave? Option A: writers bump refcount (CAS) before commit. Option B: writers forward to draining owner for short window.
Mira: Forwarding seems easier to start with. Bump/CAS would be ideal long-term but needs atomic lease-store ops.
ops-bot: Deploy note: prototype non-durable drain with forwarding on 2% canary tonight 01:00 UTC.
Rachel: Observability checklist: drain.started, drain.persisted, drain.tookover, drain.completed(reason), write.forwarded, router.negative_cache_hit.
Kai: Router negative cache on rejection is important to avoid thundering retries. Add header X-Prefix-Draining and let routers cache per-epoch for 15s.
Noah: Memory caps: global_drain_bytes and per_tenant_drain_bytes. If admit would breach caps, we convert to immediate evict.
Mira: Also add a fail-safe: max_drain_time. If exceeded, force completion to avoid indefinite memory hold from slow writers.
Rachel: Playbook: rollback if p99 tail increases >0.5% or any RA-write inconsistency observed. We'll add a small correctness test in Canaries that injects owner crashes during drains.
Mira: I'll write a short RFC with state machine and experiment config. Thanks team.
